test(shop): the P0 publish wiring gets its tests, and two review findings land

Codex review of e875ff01: (1) the approve→publish path had no UI test —
three now drive the REAL hooks against a fake shopRpc and functions.invoke:
a successful approve publishes exactly once for that product; a publish
failure leaves the recorded approve visible, raises its own message, and
the retry button re-invokes; request-changes never touches the worker.
(2) VariantEditor tracked blur-touched groups by index, so deleting group i
handed its touched state to whichever group slid into slot i — removeGroup
now shifts the set with the rows. (3, contested with evidence) the
suggested publish-commit race cannot corrupt state: products carries
CHECK products_publish_requires_approval (is_published=false OR
status='approved'), so a reopen racing the worker ends in a loud 23514 and
the retry button, not needs_changes+published.

Also: the client import in usePublishProduct goes lazy — client.ts throws
at module load without env vars, which is what failed CI quality on
e875ff01 through the MediaEditor test import chain.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(shop): Wave 0 round 2 — approve now publishes, and anon lost the base tables

P0: approving a product moved the state machine and nothing else — no
client anywhere called the shop-media-lifecycle publish action, so every
approved product stayed invisible with its media in draft, and the admin
screen reported exactly that with no button to press. Approve now triggers
the publish call (the RPC itself still does not publish — the acceptance
tests pin that), and an approved-but-not-visible product shows a 'Đưa lên
sàn' retry button, which also serves the reopen → approve cycle.

P1 (migration 20260815090000): the anon key could read sku+stock_on_hand,
products.internal_note, decided_by and draft_path straight off the base
tables — RLS scopes rows, never columns, and the TO-public policies existed
only because public_products was security_invoker. The view is now DEFINER
(its WHERE and column list are the boundary), the three public policies are
dropped, and anon loses SELECT on the base tables outright: the Wave-0
probe answers 42501. Twelve new pgTAP assertions pin it (red-proved); four
legacy suites moved to the stronger contract, full suite 1403/1403.

P2: /shop and the PDP claimed ThePickleHub verifies sellers' papers — the
pilot collects none. Both now state what actually happens.

Also, from the same test pass: raw enums labelled (SECTION_LABEL /
STATUS_LABEL, the page <title> included); category and admin-tab count
chips get their missing CSS rule; group-value errors wait for blur instead
of flashing mid-typing (validity still blocks Save live); the status
timeline overrides the app-wide refetchOnMount:false so a resubmit shows
its milestone without a hard reload; an ACTIVE seller is routed to the
seller channel instead of 'Bắt đầu đăng ký'; the seller-home overview stops
calling the products screen 'sắp có'.

Coverage 83.76% (denominator +93, new code carries its tests); bundle
1950.1/1970 KB.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(shop): Wave 0 findings — the admin frame could not scroll, and three rough edges

P0: .tl-admin-frame clipped both axes inside a 100dvh shell, so review
content taller than the frame had no scrollbar anywhere — mouse wheel dead,
only Tab and programmatic scrollIntoView reached the decision panel. The
X-axis clip stays (it exists to contain wide tables); the body is now the
Y scroller, with min-height:0 on the grid items so it may be shorter than
its content, and an auto-1fr row split on mobile.

Also from the same session: the review screen showed raw enums (ca-nhan,
submitted) where the queue already spoke Vietnamese — both now share one
label map in applicationState; the decision radios carry accessible names
instead of announcing 'on'; and Seller Rules v1 renders as readable
markup (headings, lists, quotes — a ~70-line renderer, React-escaped, no
markdown dependency at 20KB of bundle headroom) with the approval-desk
metadata table dropped from DISPLAY only — the stored body that acceptances
sign keeps its bytes and hash.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(shop-pilot): teardown deletes exact object names from the catalog, not folder prefixes

The seventh storage-teardown lie: the list endpoint returns one level of
folders, and remove() on those prefixes answers HTTP 200 having deleted
nothing — 13 objects survived a 'clean' run. Names now come straight from
storage.objects and the remaining count is read back after the delete.
Final counts: every fixture counter zero, including storage.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

test(shop-pilot): CP27 harness — the acceptance run as it actually happened

The full cp27-run harness, committed with every correction tonight's run
forced: chain-a1 speaks shop_application_decide's vocabulary
(request-changes, f-desc/f-addr targets); chain-a2 writes like the
production client (return=minimal), reads shop_contact_channels.state and
calls shop_contact_decide(_id,...) pinning the 6-arg overload; chain-b2
reads media under product.media; activate-shop covers the admin activation
step (pending_activation → active through the shops_update_admin policy —
the run proved product_create refuses before it); finish-17e re-establishes
the 17e verdict after a platform blip (SUPABASE_EDGE_RUNTIME_SERVICE_DEGRADED,
one 503 at 14:17+07) killed the poll mid-loop; teardown sweeps the rewound
shop's prefixes too and expects ledger 360. The resume-* runners document
the phase-wise re-entry used tonight; secrets.local.json, registry.json and
logs stay gitignored.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(shop): StepBody remounted on every render, killing focus each time the form re-rendered

The real root of CP27 case 8: StepBody is defined inside the component, so
<StepBody /> hands React a new element type on every render and the whole
step subtree is unmounted and remounted for every state change. The deep
link DID focus the field (the two earlier fixes made sure the timer waits
for the form) — and lost it half a second later when the next query settled
and re-rendered. A hand-typing user loses focus the same way; automated
fill() never sees it because it writes the value in one event. Calling
StepBody() inlines the JSX with no component boundary, so the DOM nodes
survive re-renders.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(shop): gate the deep-link focus on every query the form waits for

Round 2 of the CP27 case 8 fix: the first gate covered remote.isLoading but
the form also waits for the pilot-access query, and on the deep-link click
that was the one still in flight — the 60ms focus timer fired against the
LoadingState skeleton and never re-armed. The effect now mirrors the render
gate exactly (pilot AND application loaded) so it re-fires when the form is
really on screen.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(shop): the moderator's deep link focused nothing on a cold load

CP27 case 8: /seller/application?step=N&focus=<field> ran its focus effect
against the loading skeleton — focusField found no element and returned
silently, and the effect's deps never re-fired it once the data arrived. So
the deep link moved focus only when the application draft happened to be
cached, which is exactly the class of bug the VI anchors shipped once
already. The effect is now gated on remote.isLoading and re-fires when the
form really exists.

Harness: case 8 now clicks the per-field deep link (the first revision
matched the generic edit button by text and reported the deep link broken
without ever clicking it), asserts the focused element IS the field named in
the href, and cp27-run gains the resume-from-7 runner used tonight.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(shop): the applicant could read the moderator's internal_note off the base table

CP27 case 6c, against staging: every production call site reads through
my_shop_application (which has no internal_note column), but the base table
still granted SELECT on every column to authenticated and select_own hands
the applicant their row — so one hand-written REST call returned the
moderator's note verbatim. pgTAP never saw it because every assertion
exercised the view or the RPCs, not a bare table read.

Same shape as the cleanup-health fix (20260814130000): revoke at the layer
the request hits. authenticated keeps SELECT on every column except
internal_note, so select=* on the table now answers 42501 for sellers and
admins alike; the moderation screens move to shop_applications_admin, a
definer view gated by is_admin() (aal2) — the boundary the decide RPC
already trusts. Writes untouched; service_role untouched.

Regression: shop_application_internal_note_privacy.test.sql (10 assertions,
red-proved: re-granting the table turns 3 red). shop_phase1_rls updated
where the security got stronger than its assertions. Harness: chain-a1 sent
product_decide's vocabulary (request_changes) to shop_application_decide,
which takes request-changes — the 22023 it got back is what stopped the
suite one case before this leak. teardown now expects ledger 360.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(shop-pilot): CP27 17e — monotonic clock for the 400s bound

Codex round 4: Date.now() is non-monotonic, a forward clock jump could
falsely satisfy the worker wall-clock wait. performance.now() cannot.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
